bilateral renal cell carcinoma in an asymmetrically horseshoe kidney, with the tumor located in the upper and lower pole, can be accurately assessed preoperatively with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and digital subtraction angiogram (DSA).

the preoperative imaging of a horseshoe-kidney carcinoma.

the best preoperative imaging of a horseshoe renal carcinoma is obtained with a combination of MRI and digital subtraction arteriography.

the combination of magnetic resonance imaging and digital subtraction angiographic studies is the optimal method for the preoperative assessment and planning of the surgical approach for renal cell carcinoma in horseshoe kidneys.

MRI is the method of choice for preoperative planning in horseshoe kidneys with tumor, but that digital subtraction angiography is mandatory for the preoperative planning in cases where a nephron sparing resection has to be considered.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
preoperative imaging with MRI and angiography in a horseshoes kidney is mandatory to achieve optimal preservation of renal function and to minimize morbidity.
MRI is the best imaging technique to assess the horseshoe kidney and its tumors.
the combination of magnetic resonance imaging and digital subtraction angiogram is the most accurate imaging modality for the preoperative assessment of horseshoe kidney with renal cell carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
preoperative planning in a horseshoes kidney should include a thorough assessment of the tumor and the vascular supply.
the imaging modality used should be chosen according to the specific clinical question.
